key_insight: Replace geometry-driven level-of-detail tokenization with a learned, multi-scale semantic tokenization (LoST) so 3D shapes are represented by fewer, semantically meaningful tokens that are better suited for autoregressive generative models.
problem_solved: Current 3D tokenization relies on spatial LoD hierarchies designed for rendering/compression, which produce many redundant, token-inefficient representations that hurt autoregressive generation quality, scalability, and control.
method: Learn a hierarchy of semantic groupings across scales to produce tokens that represent parts and structural semantics rather than raw geometric patches.
Construct a Level-of-Semantics token hierarchy (LoST) to replace geometric LoD; emit compact multi-scale tokens for each shape.
Plug LoST tokens into autoregressive generative pipelines, reducing token count while improving generation fidelity and controllability.
impact: LoST makes autoregressive 3D generation more token- and compute-efficient, improving quality, speed, and downstream editing/conditioning capabilities—enabling larger models and datasets to be used practically.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: geometric LoD tokenization vs LoST semantic tokenization with token overlays on a 3D model and token counts.
Pipeline flowchart: 3D input → LoST encoder → semantic token hierarchy → autoregressive generator → reconstructed/generated shape.
Bar chart comparing token counts, generation quality (e.g., FID or IoU), and inference time for LoD vs LoST.
Heatmapped 3D render showing semantic tokens/parts (different colors) to illustrate interpretability and controllability.
paper_title: LoST: Level of Semantics Tokenization for 3D Shapes
paper_authors: Niladri Shekhar Dutt, Zifan Shi, Paul Guerrero, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Duygu Ceylan
